groups.title: Antacid Oral Liquid
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for acid reflux, heartburn and indigestion caused by reflux of stomach contents (for example after meals or during pregnancy).
groups.usage: For people aged 12 years and over and adults, 10 to 20 mL 4 times a day, after meals and at bedtime.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine. Before taking it, patients with congestive heart failure and other conditions requiring sodium restriction should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Acid reflux, heartburn, indigestion from reflux of stomach contents
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 12 years; congestive heart failure; sodium restriction

groups.title: Anti-inflammatory Enzyme Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve inflammatory swelling after surgery or injury and in milk stasis.
groups.usage: For adults, 2 tablets 4 times a day on the first day, then a maintenance dose of 1 tablet 4 times a day. Much about the mechanism of action in the body is still unexplained and the dose-effect relationship has not been established, so do not take it without a clear purpose.
groups.caution: Do not take if you have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or a genetic problem such as glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Inflammatory swelling after surgery or injury; milk stasis
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Galactose intolerance and related genetic problems

groups.title: Cold Relief Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 2 capsules per dose; for people aged 8 years to under 15 years, 1 capsule per dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Anti-inflammatory Analgesic Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used as supportive treatment for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthropathy, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after trauma or surgery, and infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 tablet (300 mg) 2 to 4 times a day. Do not exceed 4 tablets (1200 mg) a day.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause gastrointestinal bleeding. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Vitamin D Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used as supportive treatment for osteoporosis and to prevent the risk of vitamin D deficiency disease in healthy people without malabsorption.
groups.usage: As supportive treatment for osteoporosis, take 1 tablet (1000 IU) once a day. To prevent the risk of vitamin D deficiency disease and to prevent rickets, take 1/2 tablet (500 IU) once a day. Adults take it with plenty of water. For young children who find the tablet hard to swallow, place the tablet on a spoon, let it disintegrate in water and give it with a meal where possible. When adding it to food, add it after the food has been boiled, and the dose may need adjusting if the food is rich in vitamin D.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, have high blood calcium, high urine calcium or kidney stones, are an infant under 3 months, or have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or a related genetic problem. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Supportive treatment for osteoporosis; prevention of vitamin D deficiency
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 3 months; high blood or urine calcium; kidney stones

groups.title: Antihistamine Decongestant Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion and watery eyes caused by a head cold and by allergic or vasomotor rhinitis.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 tablet per dose; for children aged 12 to 14 years, 1/2 tablet per dose, 3 times a day after meals.
groups.caution: If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion and watery eyes from a cold or rhinitis

groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, or have liver cirrhosis, cystathionine synthase deficiency, peptic ulcer or severe renal impairment. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Low-dose Aspirin Enteric-coated Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction and unstable angina, and after coronary artery bypass grafting.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 tablet once a day. As this is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before a meal with plenty of water.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine or to other salicylates, or if you have peptic ulcer, aspirin-induced asthma or a history of it, or haemophilia. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Prevention of thrombus formation; cardiovascular risk reduction

groups.title: Laxative Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for constipation and for the loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, abnormal intestinal fermentation and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 1 to 2 tablets 2 times a day, morning and evening, on an empty stomach (before meals or between meals). groups.caution: Do not take if you have an acute abdominal condition (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and similar) or intestinal obstruction. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
